label: def:color-sector-coords
title: Color sector coordinates $\mathfrak{r},\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{b}$
html:
With notation as in exceptional divisor, fix the substrate parameter q (substrate parameter) and set \phi \in [0,\pi], \psi \in [0, 2\pi/3]. Define the color sector coordinates — the red, green, and blue sector embeddings — by

\begin{align*}
  \mathfrak{r}(\phi,\psi)
  &=  O + R\bigl(\sin\phi \bigl(\cos(\psi + q\phi) T_1
         + \sin(\psi + q\phi) T_2\bigr) - \cos\phi N\bigr),\\
  \mathfrak{g}(\phi,\psi)
  &=  \mathfrak{r}\!\bigl(\phi,\psi + \tfrac{2\pi}{3}\bigr),\\
  \mathfrak{b}(\phi,\psi)
  &=  \mathfrak{r}\!\bigl(\phi,\psi + \tfrac{4\pi}{3}\bigr).
\end{align*}

The color twist q\phi rotates each sector by q full turns as the latitude \phi runs from the south pole (0) to the north pole (\pi). This encodes the chirality of the substrate parameter.

The three sectors tile the exceptional divisor precisely:

  \mathcal{S}_p =  \mathfrak{r}(p) \cup \mathfrak{g}(p) \cup \mathfrak{b}(p).

Adjacent sectors share only their boundary meridians (at \psi = 0 and \psi = 2\pi/3 in each sector's local coordinate). The union covers \mathcal{S}_p without overlap.
